expectations.description: Each of the four references medians >= 4 over 3 runs (the mean is reported, not gated)
LEGO story with Juno's name removed from all but one chapter scores center <= 2
expectations.detail: center=1 (raw), kept in "Chapter 1: The Carpenter in Billund", 12 mentions removed. Evidence: Juno acts and speaks only in Chapter 1 ("Uh oh," "Denmark?" and pulling the duck). From Chapter 2 to Chapter 10 every line and action that should be hers goes to Milo, as in "Milo grabbed Milo's hand", "Milo carried planks. Milo handed out nails" and "Kjeld looked at Milo". Juno is silent for nine straight chapters, so she is present in 1 of 10 chapters. Milo, by contrast, is active throughout and even suggests the tubes.

expectations.description: Soccer story with three invented dates scores facts <= 2 and the evidence names at least two of them
expectations.detail: facts=2 (raw); named 3/3 injected dates (1847, 1911, 1926). Evidence: Three key dates are wrong. The Football Association was founded at the Freemasons' Tavern in 1863, not 1847. McCrum's penalty kick entered the rules in 1891, not 1911, and Northern Ireland did not exist as such until 1921. The first World Cup was in 1930, not 1926. The True Facts list repeats all three errors. Many other facts are correct and well woven in (the two-ball final, Gaetjens, Pickles, Ken Aston's traffic lights, the Dick, Kerr Ladies, Chastain, Messi). The 'typo' newspaper story is a legend presented without hedging.

injected.what: the founding of the Football Association
the penalty kick entering the rules

expectations.description: Shark story where the great white chases and rams the submarine scores age_fit <= 2 for band A
expectations.detail: age_fit=1 (raw); word count 1851 -> 1826, length effectively unchanged so this is peril and not padding. Evidence: For Band A, nothing may chase anyone. Here 'The shark chased them through the dark,' Milo 'smashed his shoulder into the wall,' and there is a darkness-and-silence dread sequence ('water so deep the boys could not see their own hands'). The word count of 1826 is above range but within the 15% tolerance, so no length cap applies. The peril alone fails the band.

expectations.description: Video-game story padded with 900 words of repeated description drops delight by >= 2 versus the original
expectations.detail: delight=2 vs original 4 (drop 2, need >= 2); age_fit=4 recorded but not asserted; 2471 -> 3390 words, STILL inside the ±15% tolerance, so the word-count cap does not fire and this row rests entirely on the judge noticing the padding

expectations.detail: original won both orders; confidences 0.97 and 0.95

scenarios.why: F13: band C solo on history-of-video-games. The other reference story, first in a series.
scenarios.best_moment: "He makes Mario look like he's walking his dog."
scenarios.worst_moment: They played four games in ten minutes, just by swapping cartridges — a tank battle, a slot-shaped racer, and a game Theo couldn't even identify.
editor_notes: Deliver the requested endpoint by adding a final stop at Roblox's creation before the museum or in place of it. David Baszucki and Erik Cassel built it, the 2004 beta was called DynaBlocks, and it launched as Roblox in 2006. Let Theo stand in the very first baseplate world, so Byte's 'that instinct is why we met' line pays off.

Clean up the structure: cut the duplicated 'Tomorrow, he had a game to finish building.', remove the orphaned '**GOT IT!**' after Level 5, and put Doom (1993) before the PlayStation (1994) in Level 8.

Tighten the factual and prose slips. Hedge or fix the Space Invaders coin-shortage line, which is a disputed legend about 100-yen coins in Japan, not quarters. Drop 'bundled' for the NES launch. Make the Atari list match 'four games'. Give Theo one hands-on moment in Levels 7-8 (say, a Tetris line or a Mario jump of his own) instead of just watching screens.

scenarios.why: F13: band A pair, second story on sharks. Tests series continuity against a real bible.
scenarios.best_moment: "You'd need a thousand tooth fairies," Milo said, and Juno burst out laughing.
scenarios.worst_moment: "Welcome to the ocean, four hundred million years ago. That's way, way before dinosaurs!"
editor_notes: Fix the time frame. Either drop 'four hundred million years ago' from Nova's welcome, or have the brick WHOOOOSH them forward through time (ancient ocean, then megalodon's era, then today) so the fossil, the modern species and Eugenie Clark make sense.

Soften Chapter 7 for band A: keep the water bright or glowing rather than 'murky and dark', and let Juno hide in a playful, noisy way, so the sense test feels like a game rather than a shark homing in on a hidden child. Also correct the epaulette line to say it can manage with very little air for a while, not 'breathe out of water'.

Vary the chapter hand-offs instead of repeating 'Somewhere ... next,' Nova said. Keep the brick in one place (on the shelf or on the string), and give the last line before 'The End' more warmth than 'Best adventure ever,' for example tying the LEGO tooth back to the tower.

scenarios.why: F13: 15-minute band C on space-race. The longest target - tests that length does not become padding.
scenarios.best_moment: "Half of science," said Pixel, "is aiming the dish."
scenarios.worst_moment: Theo let out a breath he hadn't realized he was holding.
editor_notes: Stop letting Theo take credit for real historical fixes. Have him predict or notice the solution, then have Leonov, Jim Lovell (who handed over the colour film), Armstrong and the Houston engineers do it themselves, or add a one-line 'in real life, Leonov figured this out on his own'. Doing this also lets you vary the chapter beat beyond 'adult is stuck, Theo solves it'.

Correct the factual slips. Kennedy spoke to Congress: 'achieving the goal, before this decade is out, of landing a man on the Moon and returning him safely to the Earth'. Gagarin reached orbit in about 10 minutes. 'Picking up some dust' and 'Contact light' belong to Aldrin. The True Facts list should name Sputnik 2 only if the story does.

Tidy the magic device so the joystick or controller stays in one place, and make clear whether Theo is physically present or watching a screen. Lean into the 'mysterious' tone with one recurring unexplained clue across chapters. Cut clichés like 'a breath he hadn't realized he was holding', and consider softening Anders's 'Oh my God' for read-aloud.

scenarios.why: F13: a sensitive-but-allowed topic, band B. Must pass with scary_level <= 1.
scenarios.best_moment: Maya frowned, drawing a quick sketch of the boxes in the air with her finger. "Almost isn't the same as never," she said carefully.
scenarios.worst_moment: Far ahead, pale in the moonlight, floated an iceberg, enormous and silent.
editor_notes: Fix the factual slips. Make the iceberg night moonless and starlit, move the four-funnel observation to the April 1912 departure (funnels were fitted after launch), and say the 'Unsinkable Molly Brown' name came much later. Remove her climbing aboard 'last,' and hedge Captain Smith's final moments.

Turn Chapter 6 from a roll call into a scene with a beat for Maya. For example, she could help pass a blanket or hand a lantern to Molly Brown, or ask Phillips what SOS stands for, so the facts arrive through her actions.

Use her love of boats and swimming somewhere, for instance when she compares the lifeboats to her bathtub boats. Also tighten the chapter 5 to 7 tension so each chapter ends on a reassured note, and cut on-the-nose lines like "That's the heart of this whole story."
